problem: Timing _regular_user_shape alone can overstate eliminable wall because that prewalk may warm filesystem metadata for the immediately following Builder.scan.
question: When exact shape facts are gifted and _regular_user_shape returns them without a filesystem walk, does promoted-r24 outer create wall actually fall while final bytes and release policy facts stay identical?
mechanism: Monkeypatch only base _regular_user_shape. Mature control executes it normally. Gifted arm returns the exact (regular_files, largest_regular_bytes) facts previously established for the same accepted source without walking that source during the measured build. Both arms call promoted release_product._locality_bounded_r24_build.
simpler_control: This is stronger than phase timing because it prices the downstream Builder.scan under the altered cache/work sequence rather than assuming timed prewalk wall is fully removable.
prediction: Many Tiny Files should retain a material net outer-wall saving if the duplicated metadata walk is genuinely removable; rows whose apparent phase cost is mostly cache warming should collapse toward zero net saving.
kill: If gifted-shape median outer-wall saving is nonpositive or below 10% of the inherited strict-create gap on every row, retire shape-prewalk reuse even if direct helper timing was larger.
identity_gate: Every mature/gifted output must have identical final promoted archive bytes/SHA-256 and identical regular-file/locality/micro-pack/wide-policy facts.
boundary: Gifted shape is an oracle and earns no product credit. A positive result only justifies implementation work that discovers/reuses those facts generically and preserves mutable-source semantics.
